anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, REG2 pin 30 is drawn as PVIN_8 but is attached to local label NET0049. NET0049 is also the switch-node net used by pins 4 SW_1, 9 SW_2, 10 SW_3, 11 SW_4, 12 SW_5, and 29 SW_6, and it feeds the bootstrap/inductor node. The other PVIN pins (13-19, 27, 28) are on NET0040, the input rail.
anomalies.expected: PVIN_8 is a power-input pin of the MIC26903 buck regulator and should be tied to the battery/input rail (NET0040/VCC), like the other PVIN pins, not to the switching node.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: REG2 MIC26903YJL-TR shows '30 PVIN_8 < NET0049' while pins 4, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 29 are also labeled 'NET0049'.
Main buck regulator (5 V rail) | Hades (top sheet) | Microchip MIC26903YJL-TR

anomalies.impact: This shorts one of the buck regulator's input power pins to the switching node. During the low-side phase of the converter this can create a direct low-impedance path from the input rail to ground, preventing proper 5 V regulation and likely damaging the regulator or input supply.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains a power-stage anomaly: the MIC26903 buck regulator's PVIN_8 pin is connected to the switch-node net NET0049 instead of the input rail NET0040, which would bridge input and switching node and break the 5 V regulator.
